source_title: Spirited Away / 千と千尋の神隠し (2001 Studio Ghibli film)
continuity_scope: Studio Ghibli's original 2001 animated feature, Japanese title 千と千尋の神隠し and official English title Spirited Away, written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki; Japanese release 20 July 2001, approximately 125 minutes. The selected witnesses are Studio Ghibli's official work profile and GKIDS's official original-film release/synopsis page. Manga/storyboard books, stage productions, games, merchandise, translated/dubbed tracks, and all adaptations are separate witnesses; the GKIDS page notes Japanese and English audio as release options, not proof that their dialogue/name rendering is identical to all versions.
work_or_witnesses: Hayao Miyazaki, Spirited Away / 千と千尋の神隠し, Studio Ghibli original animated feature (2001)
Studio Ghibli official work profile; GKIDS official film synopsis/release information
coverage_rule: All named individual dramatic figures in the selected official film synopsis: Chihiro and Yubaba. Chihiro's parents, bathhouse workers, spirits/demons, and other figures are unnamed in the selected evidence window and are not nodes. Spirits/yōkai-adjacent categories, bathhouse roles, transformations, magic, items, places, and themes are dimensions or terms.
omissions: All named or unnamed figures outside the exact official synopsis, including Chihiro's parents, bathhouse workers, Haku, and all other familiar characters without claim-level evidence in this selected window.

Detailed film scenes, identity/name changes, individual spirit taxonomy, later outcomes, storyboards, books, stage versions, games, merchandise, English/Japanese dub dialogue differences, and adaptations.
Fan wikis, Wikipedia, databases, reviews, social summaries, and long script/frame reproduction.
uncertainties: The official sources establish the Japanese and English film-title pair, but the selected profile/synopsis does not provide Japanese-script or alternate localized character names. Chihiro and Yubaba are retained in the exact English-source form; no Sen, Haku, or other alias is imported.

Fantastic spirits, demons, magical bathhouse imagery, and transformation are source-fiction terms. The selected evidence does not establish a one-to-one Shinto, yōkai, kami, or living-religion equivalence; none is asserted.

The premise includes child separation/peril, coerced labor in a magical bathhouse, parental transformation, and frightening supernatural imagery. These are fictional content cautions, not labor, child-safety, religious, or medical guidance.
evidence_basis: Official Studio Ghibli original-film profile and GKIDS official film synopsis/release page only. No fan or secondary source is used as canonical evidence.
